concepts.title: Urban Local Bodies
concepts.definition: Cities and towns are run by urban local bodies, elected municipal councils and corporations that provide services like water, roads, waste removal and street lights for millions of residents.
concepts.key_idea: A city's needs are too many for any one office: elected local bodies divide the work ward by ward.

concepts.title: Municipal Corporations and Municipal Councils
concepts.definition: Big cities are governed by municipal corporations, smaller towns by municipal councils and nagar panchayats; each is elected, raises local taxes and keeps records for its area.
concepts.key_idea: The size of the settlement decides the shape of its body: corporations for metropolises, councils for towns.

concepts.title: Wards and Councillors in a City
concepts.definition: Each city is divided into wards, and every ward elects a councillor; councillors together form the municipal body, decide budgets and bye-laws, and answer to the ward's residents.
concepts.key_idea: Wards shrink a huge city to a human scale: every locality gets one voice in the civic body.

concepts.title: Participatory Democracy in Cities
concepts.definition: Urban governance aims at participatory democracy: citizens, not just officials, take part in city functioning through elections, ward meetings and feedback, so that administration stays answerable to residents.
concepts.key_idea: Good city governance empowers citizens to participate, not merely to receive services.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does urban governance need to be more complex than rural?

solution_template.explain: Cities gather lakhs of people of many languages, trades and neighbourhoods.
Water, traffic, waste and housing at that scale need layered bodies, from wards to corporations.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How is a ward like a constituency in miniature?

solution_template.explain: A ward is a small slice of the city with clear boundaries.
Its elected councillor carries local problems to the civic body, just as an MLA carries a constituency's voice to the assembly.
